note: I rated 541b4ef + 87fd59a (w22 ink print). Builds: /tmp/b1 (w21) and /tmp/b2 (w22). Renders: scratchpad/r1 and r2. My comparison sheets are in scratchpad/raters/monoA2/: cmp.jpg (f40 | f13 | aisle w21 | aisle w22 | seated w21 | seated w22) and wall.jpg (2x wall crops: f40, aisle w21 / w22, seated w21 / w22). I made no new renders because the machine is loaded and ink_aisle / ink_seated are already final-colour. q11 / q19 / q13 are unchanged, so I carry their scores over from w21. My measurements (PIL; p5-p95 of the channel mean): ink_aisle (320-600 x 300-410) w21 L199 range 30 h42 s0.090 B/R 0.910 -> w22 L192 range 29 h41 s0.085 B/R 0.915. ink_seated (200-470 x 215-300) w21 L197 range 36 s0.084 -> w22 L191 range 28 h42 s0.079 B/R 0.921. Photos: f13 L204 range 24 s0.114; f40 L191 range 34 s0.111. Mean luminance gradient rose about 10 % in x (0.82 -> 0.93 aisle, 0.81 -> 0.88 seated), so the edges are crisper. Result: the strata are now thinner and more numerous and break into ragged, stair-stepped fragments, which is much nearer f40's dry-brush stipple than w21's rounded blobs. Value, contrast and hue stay inside the photo band. The trade-off: the wall is now covered by fairly even, full-width horizontal bands. In f40 the bands are fewer and bigger, with large light-ground gaps between cloud masses (a low-frequency envelope), and the stipple sits inside those masses. As a result the w22 wall reads slightly busier and a touch greyer overall (L -7) than the photo. It is a net gain, small. Lighting is noted, not scored: the render's cool-neutral ceiling still makes the wall read warmer than in the photos.

details.detail: F front wall ink print (q03 / q05 via ink_aisle, ink_seated)
details.note: Was 8.6. The fragmented stipple strata now match f40's texture character. The remaining gap is composition: the bands are too uniform and dense, with too little open light ground between large cloud masses, and the mean is a touch dark (L191-192 against f13's 204).

details.detail: Door-2 welcome galley / aft ash wall
F front wall, flight-deck door, door 1 (q01)

issues.detail: Strata too even: no large-scale cloud envelope
issues.problem: In w22 the cloud bands run across the full wall width at a near-regular pitch with similar density, so the wall reads as a striped, slightly busy grey. In f40 / f13 there are 2-3 large cloud masses, each built from stipple strata, with broad areas of open light ground between them (the upper-right and lower-centre of f40 are mostly ground). For the same reason the mean L sits at 191-192, against f13's 204.
issues.evidence: wall.jpg row 1 (f40) against rows 3 and 5 (w22). ink_seated L191 against f13 L204, f40 L191.
issues.fix: In inkPanel, multiply the stratum mask by a low-frequency envelope, for example env = smoothstep(0.35, 0.65, fbm(x/2.5, y/0.6, seed2)), so that about 35-40 % of the wall is open ground. Keep the edge ramp and speckle as they are. Expect the mean L to rise about 5-8 while the range stays at 25-35.

issues.detail: Hue still slightly warm in context
issues.problem: The absolute B/R is 0.92, against the photo's 0.89. The difference is fine; the residual warmth against the render's neutral ceiling is lighting's call.
issues.fix: No monuments change. Integrator note only.
